text: Root-type long radish needs light, loose, well-drained soil to grow straight, unblemished roots — sandy loam and river-deposited alluvial soil (ដ៘ទន្លេ) are best. Heavy, poorly drained black/clay soils are unsuitable, as they restrict root elongation and can cause deformed roots. (Leaf-type radish, by contrast, tolerates the reddish-brown highland/lateritic soils common in Cambodia reasonably well, but this source's focus — root-type long radish — specifically needs the lighter soil types described above.)
